note: From the OpenStreetMap main API export (tools/osm-to-kit.mjs, 13 October 2026), at real scale across the line like the tracks: two side platforms about 107 m long in a cutting on the Marple line, 1.68 m outside its two tracks (platform 1, towards Manchester, is the halt's; OSM maps the line's centreline a track's width off the corridor here, so its parts across the line are moved over to the tracks), the footbridge over the line 15 m beyond the platforms' north end with a path down the cutting side behind each platform to it (drawn as a ramp from each platform's middle), the booking office at street level beside The Link, and The Link's road bridge over the line north of it. Positive v is north-east; the booking office is on the south-west side. The view from above (docs/reference/aerial/brinnington.jpg) shows the cutting through the estate, wooded on both sides. Photos (docs/reference/photos/brinnington: entrance-1.jpg, platform-2.jpg and overview-1.jpg Gerald England 2026, entrance-2.jpg and overview-2.jpg Graham Hogg 2015, platform-1.jpg Kevin Waterhouse 2024, shelter-1.jpg JThomas 2013, roadbridge-1.jpg John Topping 2013): the booking office is a low 1977 brick box with a glazed front under a shallow canopy, at road level (the `street` flag); the footbridge is blue, drawn as the usual enclosed one; The Link's bridge is a plain deck on concrete abutments with red railings (drawn in rust); each platform has a small open-fronted brick shelter (drawn as the usual glazed shelter); tall pale lamp columns. No canopy, lifts or car park in the photos (kerbside parking only): the canopy, the lifts, the platform extensions at the south end, the kiosk and the snack bar are the game's. The Middlesex Road / The Link bus stop is a short walk south-west; the replacement bus stop on The Link by the booking office is from memory, placed by eye, as are the cycle stands. Departure boards on each platform. Real scale (13 October 2026): everything across the line (v, outlines, rails, widths across) divided by 1.25 from the 1.25 times real it was drawn at, so the kit stands on its real footprint and lines up with the real buildings round it.
